title: Public-coin lower bound from a distributional hypothesis
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Suppose every deterministic one-way protocol for the Index function on $n$-bit strings and indices in $[n]$, with Boolean output and cost at most $\lfloor n/10\rfloor$, has error strictly greater than $1/8$ under the uniform distribution on input pairs. Then the one-way public-coin communication complexity of the Index function at error $1/8$ is strictly greater than $\lfloor n/10\rfloor$.
hypotheses_covered: Every deterministic one-way protocol for Index with cost at most $\lfloor n/10\rfloor$ has uniform-distributional error strictly greater than $1/8$
replaced:
If every deterministic one-way protocol for $\mathrm{IND}_n$ of cost at most
$\lfloor n/10 \rfloor$ has uniform-distributional error greater than $1/8$, then the
public-coin one-way communication complexity of $\mathrm{IND}_n$ at error $1/8$ is strictly
greater than $\lfloor n/10 \rfloor$.  This is the previous theorem specialised to the source's
constants $\varepsilon = 1/8$, $c = \lfloor n/10 \rfloor$.
